transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 10:30 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CS), Samira Lee (Redwood SRE), Priya Rao (Atlas Platform), Ethan Cole (Atlas SRE), Lina Park (Atlas Secops), Mark Donnelly (CTO)

[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: hey priya here.
[00:06] Ethan: ethan, s-r-e.
[00:07] Lina: lina on secops.
[00:09] Mark: mark, cto.
[00:11] Marco: marco from redwood se.
[00:12] Jordan: jordan, cs.
[00:13] Samira: samira, redwood infra.
[00:15] Alyssa: awesome. agenda - give a quick status on the VPC pilot, go over the latency numbers Marco collected, discuss the intermittent egress failures priya flagged, and then next steps. anything else?
[00:23] Priya: nothing else from me. would like some clarity on upgrade and canary paths too - we had that question last week.

---

[03:12] Marco: ok so quick on benchmarks: we ran the end-to-end generator tests you asked for inside the customer VPC using the test harness. results were - p50 ~60ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~480ms for the larger contexts (3k tokens). after adjusting batching and enabling KV prefix caching we saw p95 drop to ~150ms but p99 still spikes around 420-500 on bursts. note: those numbers include network egress within the VPC path and the model execution time.
[03:50] Ethan: those numbers look okay on p95 but p99 is concerning for our user-facing flows. do you have a breakdown of where that tail is coming from? network vs kernel vs queuing?
[04:05] Marco: yeah we captured traces - about 60% of tail is queuing during short bursts when our autoscaler is spinning up warm workers; about 30% is kernel/quantization overhead for long contexts, rest is network jitter from NAT timeout retries. I'll attach the trace logs.
[04:28] Priya: we saw some 504s last week during a synthetic load test, that might be related.
[04:34] Marco: yep, which brings us to the routing issue - the team noticed intermittent egress failures when the pilot routes traffic through a public NAT gateway in the customer's account. based on the logs, some flows are hitting ephemeral port exhaustion and causing retries.
[04:50] Lina: can you clarify - are you using VPC peering or PrivateLink? we had concerns about peering because of cross-account routing rules.
[04:58] Samira: currently the pilot is set up with VPC peering and a NAT gateway for egress to the Redwood control plane; PrivateLink wasn't enabled because of initial infra constraints.
[05:10] Priya: ok that matches our setup. we can switch to interface VPC endpoints / PrivateLink but that requires more infra approvals from our network team.

[06:05] Marco: immediate mitigation - increase ephemeral port range on the NAT and add connection tracking timeouts. longer term, we recommend moving to PrivateLink or using dedicated egress nodes (Redwood-managed NAT) to avoid customer NAT exhaustion. PrivateLink will also improve latency variability.
[06:25] Mark: what's the security tradeoff? does PrivateLink reduce the audit surface?
[06:32] Jordan: PrivateLink keeps traffic within AWS backbone, so from an egress audit perspective it's cleaner. we can also configure flow logs and we integrate with your KMS for key wrapping; samira can follow up on KMS integration details.

[08:00] Samira: on KMS, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS or HSM. we can encrypt logs at rest and we keep an audit trail in the control plane; for private deploys we also support bringing your own key material.
[08:18] Lina: important for us - retention of audit logs and access to raw audit trails for compliance. what's the retention default?
[08:26] Jordan: default retention is 90 days for the pilot console, but we can extend or export logs to your S3 (and then you manage retention). we'll add SOC2 artifact links.

---

[12:20] Marco: back to perf tuning - KV cache hit rates were initially ~52%, after changing prompt cassification (sic) and prefix caching policy we got hit rates to ~78% which explains a lot of the p95 improvement. there are still cold misses in long-tail requests where context windows shift.
[12:45] Priya: is there a config we can tweak on our side to increase cacheability?
[12:50] Marco: yes, canonical prompts and stable prompt routing helps - avoid dynamic timestamping in prompts, use template placeholders. we can also adjust the cache TTL and the prefix match length. i'll send our recommended config values.

[14:30] Ethan: we attempted a model upgrade test yesterday - moving from the v1.2 quantized -> v1.3 optimized kernel. that caused an increase in kernel initialization time on cold workers and a couple of small 5xx errors during the canary.
[14:48] Marco: right, the upgrade path we recommend is a rolling canary - spin a small percentage of traffic to the new variant and keep automatic fallback to previous model if error rate crosses threshold. for pilot we had the canary set to 5% but our autoscaler scale up timing overlapped with the canary and created cold starts.
[15:10] Priya: can we coordinate to do upgrades during our low-traffic window and pre-warm workers?
[15:16] Samira: absolutely, we can pre-warm with a synthetic workload and stage kernels to reduce cold init. pre-warm recipes are in the doc i linked last week.

[17:05] Mark: for dedicated capacity, what's the SLA around latency and can we get guaranteed capacity for peak times?
[17:15] Alyssa: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and we can commit reserved nodes. SLA targets depend on configuration - we can offer high-priority lanes and configurable autoscaling windows. I'll include two pricing options and the associated SLOs in the follow-up.

[19:30] Priya: security question - user access: we use SSO (SAML), role-based access - can we integrate?
[19:38] Jordan: yes, we support SAML SSO and granular RBAC. we can map groups to project-level access and audit actions at token level. we'll share the mapping doc.

[22:40] Priya: one small thing - we noticed occasionally the control-plane UI would show stale token-level cost metrics; not sure if that's a cache or time-window issue.
[22:51] Jordan: yeah that's likely frontend aggregation delay; it doesn't reflect the raw logs. the token-level traces still show correct numbers. we'll sync with console infra to get that leaf fixed.

---

[25:00] Marco: quick demo - walked through trace example: showed where a request spent time in batching queue (~80ms) then kernel (~40ms) and last leg network (~30-40ms). showed two failing examples where NAT returned ``502 gateway'' during heavy NAT conn churn.
[27:12] Ethan: do you have an estimate for cost impact if we move to PrivateLink vs keeping NAT?
[27:20] Alyssa: PrivateLink has additional per-hour endpoint costs and data processing charges, but reduces retries and therefore lowers token-level compute cost from fewer retries; we'll run a sample TCO estimate and put in the deck.

[29:55] Priya: another operational ask - we need a clearly documented rollback plan if an upgrade spikes error rate.
[30:05] Marco: our rollback is automatic fallback - if the canary crosses 1% error for 5 minutes we immediately cut traffic to safe variant and notify. we can tighten or loosen thresholds based on your tolerance.

[31:40] Mark: ok looks good. i want to know for pilot success what's the threshold - do we need p95 under 200ms and p99 under 400ms?
[31:51] Priya: from product perspective p95 < 200ms is fine, but p99 needs to be under 450 for our SLA. if we can hit that with PrivateLink and pre-warming, we're happy.

[33:10] Marco: action plan summary - ramp up PrivateLink infra in staging, increase ephemeral ports as mitigation, run pre-warm before planned upgrade, re-run the full latency harness with KV cache tuned and attach traces.

[35:00] Alyssa: do we have any blockers for the next week?
[35:05] Priya: network approvals for PrivateLink - that's on us, should take 3-5 days.
[35:12] Ethan: we'll share the routing screenshots by monday.
[35:16] Priya: yep.

[36:30] Jordan: i'll upload SOC2 + network diagram to the CRM and link the security doc.

[37:10] Alyssa: great. i'll send the pricing and dedicated node options in an email and sync the proposal.

[39:00] Marco: i'll run the benchmark inside your VPC thursday and share the p95/p99 with traces. watching the autoscaler warmup will be part of that test.

[40:20] Mark: final question - any known incompatibilities with our on-prem VPN setup? some of our customers have strict firewall rules.
[40:30] Samira: generally we support site-to-site VPNs, but we need the right egress ports and longer ephemeral port ranges. we'll document the firewall rules and share with you.

[42:10] Priya: thanks, that helps.
[42:15] Alyssa: ok thanks everyone. recap: Marco runs benchmarks and shares traces (due 12/10), Priya shares routing screenshots (due 12/08), Alyssa sends pricing (due 12/05), Jordan uploads security docs (due 12/06). next sync same time next week unless network approvals delay.
[42:45] Mark: thanks all.
[42:47] Ethan: thanks.
[42:48] Lina: bye.
[42:49] Alyssa: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
